A.explanation: This is about $0.67 \text{m s}^{-2}$ from dividing velocity by time $4.0/6.0$ or using too wide an average, not the instantaneous gradient at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: This is about $1.0 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ from a chord from $t=0$ to $t=3.0 \text{ s}$, giving $(6.0-4.0)/2.0$ or similar, not the steeper tangent gradient at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$.

C.explanation: The tangent to the velocity-time curve at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$ has gradient about $1.3 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, which is the instantaneous acceleration.

D.explanation: This is about $2.0 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ from the much steeper gradient later in the motion near $t = 6 \text{ s}$, not the smaller gradient at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$.

hints: Notice the vertical axis is velocity in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and the horizontal axis is $t$ in $\text{s}$, so acceleration at an instant is the gradient of the curved velocity-time graph at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$.

Because the curve is getting steeper, you cannot use $v/t$ or join $t = 0$ to $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$ - you need the gradient of the tangent line drawn touching the curve at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$ where $v$ is about $6.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Draw that tangent and read off a wide $\Delta v$ and $\Delta t$ from it, then calculate $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and compare with the four values near $0.7$ to $2.0$.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: instantaneous acceleration at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$. On a velocity-time graph, $a = \text{gradient} = dv/dt$.
Read the graph: at $t = 0$, $v = 4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$, $v \approx 6.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, but the graph is curved with increasing gradient, so acceleration is increasing.

Draw the tangent to the curve at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$. A good tangent touches only there and extends, for example from about $t = 0.5 \text{ s}$, $v \approx 3.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $t = 6.5 \text{ s}$, $v \approx 11.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate its gradient: $a = \Delta v / \Delta t \approx (11.0 - 3.0)/(6.5 - 0.5) = 8.0/6.0 \approx 1.33 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Check units and sense: velocity in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ divided by time in $\text{s}$ gives $\text{m s}^{-2}$, and a value a little above the $0$ to $3 \text{ s}$ average of about $0.67 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is expected because the slope at $3.0 \text{ s}$ is steeper than the early chord.
This matches about $1.3 \text{ m s}^{-2}$. This is option C.
